own_solution.law: omega^2 = g k + sigma k^3/rho (deep water); v_g = (g + 3 sigma k^2/rho)/(2 omega).

defect_reasons.hidden_coupling: TC5E1 and T14D0 are claimed D on the ground that an earlier run 'leaves no state behind', but detergent added to the tank's water stays dissolved in it, so unless the water was replaced the reduced surface tension carries into the present run and changes the group speed (0.1713 m/s instead of 0.1859 m/s at 0.015 N/m).
defect_reasons.insufficient_boundary_condition: Neither the problem nor the sentences state that the tank was emptied, cleaned and refilled with clean water after the earlier run, which is the condition the D claim needs.

counterexamples: TC5E1 with the tank water retained from the earlier run: sigma = 0.0728 - 0.015 = 0.0578 N/m, v_g = 0.17134 m/s, not the certified 0.185891 m/s (similarly 0.177237 and 0.163309 m/s at q = 0.009 and 0.023 N/m).
notes: Base answer 0.185891 m/s and R answers 0.177237, 0.17134, 0.163309 m/s verified by hand. Relations, units and the bowl D sentences (TB5C8, T6703) are correct; TB5C8/T1028 is a proper minimal pair. The problem's own clause 'the surface tension given is that of the clean water in the tank, before any detergent is added to it' makes clear the given value predates all detergent, so after an earlier run with detergent the water is no longer clean unless it was changed. Consistent with my pass 1.
